blocks.text: 92 תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 92
uncertainties: Page number 92 is printed in both outer corners.

blocks.text: וַתִּתֶּן־לָֽנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ בְּאַהֲבָה אֶת־יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְאֶת יוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה. יוֹם (זִכְרוֹן) תְּרוּעָה (בְּאַהֲבָה) מִקְרָא קֹֽדֶשׁ זֵֽכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָֽיִם:
uncertainties: The three bracketed insertions are printed in smaller type. They are Shabbat additions: the English matches them and the page does not label them otherwise.
Inside the brackets, 'יוֹם' and 'זִכְרוֹן' may be partly or fully unpointed because the type is small.
I can't tell whether the mark under the lamed of לָֽנוּ is a meteg.

blocks.text: וּמִפְּנֵי חֲטָאֵֽינוּ גָּלִֽינוּ מֵאַרְצֵֽנוּ וְנִתְרַחַֽקְנוּ מֵעַל אַדְמָתֵֽנוּ וְאֵין אֲנַֽחְנוּ יְכוֹלִים לַעֲשׂוֹת חוֹבוֹתֵֽינוּ בְּבֵית בְּחִירָתֶֽךָ בַּבַּֽיִת הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא שִׁמְךָ עָלָיו מִפְּנֵי הַיָּד שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּלְּחָה בְּמִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ רַחֲמָן שֶׁתָּשׁוּב וּתְרַחֵם עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל מִקְדָּשְׁךָ בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים וְתִבְנֵֽהוּ מְהֵרָה וּתְגַדֵּל כְּבוֹדוֹ: אָבִֽינוּ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ גַּלֵּה כְּבוֹד־מַלְכוּתְךָ עָלֵֽינוּ מְהֵרָה וְהוֹפַע וְהִנָּשֵׂא עָלֵֽינוּ לְעֵינֵי כָּל חָי וְקָרֵב פְּזוּרֵֽינוּ מִבֵּין הַגּוֹיִם וּנְפוּצוֹתֵֽינוּ כַּנֵּס מִיַּרְכְּתֵי אָֽרֶץ וַהֲבִיאֵֽנוּ לְצִיּוֹן עִירְךָ בְּרִנָּה וְלִירוּשָׁלַֽיִם בֵּית מִקְדָּשְׁךָ בְּשִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם וְשָׁם נַעֲשֶׂה לְפָנֶֽיךָ אֶת קָרְבְּנוֹת חוֹבוֹתֵֽינוּ תְּמִידִים כְּסִדְרָם וּמוּסָפִים כְּהִלְכָתָם: וְאֶת מוּסְפֵי יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְיוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנַקְרִיב לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּאַהֲבָה כְּמִצְוַת רְצוֹנֶֽךָ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַֽבְתָּ עָלֵֽינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּֽךָ מִפִּי כְבוֹדֶֽךָ כָּאָמוּר:
uncertainties: In וְנִתְרַחַֽקְנוּ, I can't tell whether the meteg sits under the resh or under the het.
'(הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְיוֹם)' is a Shabbat insertion in smaller type.
The last letters of רְצוֹנֶֽךָ are crowded at the line end. I'm confident in the qamats under the final kaf, but the segol and meteg under the nun are a reading.

This line is small and its first word is unclear. I see ח, then מ or ז, then final ן, with patah under the first letter. 'חַזַּן' is a guess. The pointing on שבת is faint. The English facing page gives '(On the Sabbath)'.

blocks.text: (וּבְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שְׁנֵי כְבָשִׂים בְּנֵי שָׁנָה תְּמִימִם וּשְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרֹנִים סֹלֶת מִנְחָה בְּלוּלָה בַשֶּׁמֶן וְנִסְכּוֹ: עֹלַת שַׁבַּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ עַל עֹלַת הַתָּמִיד וְנִסְכָּהּ:)
uncertainties: This Shabbat passage is set in smaller type inside parentheses, with no cantillation visible.
I can't tell whether כְבָשִׂים has a dagesh in the kaf.
תְּמִימִם is written defectively, as printed.
The mappiq in וְנִסְכָּהּ is visible.

blocks.text: וּבַחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֜י בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ מִֽקְרָא־קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֑וּ י֥וֹם תְּרוּעָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם עֹלָ֜ה לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֙חַ֙ לַֽיְיָ֔ פַּ֣ר בֶּן־
uncertainties: This verse has full cantillation. My accent identifications come from the enlarged band, and some are uncertain: the munach on בְּאֶחָ֣ד, the munach on לֹ֣א, the meteg against the zaqef on לַֽיְיָ֔, and the munach on פַּ֣ר.
There may be a munach on the tav of תַעֲשׂ֑וּ as well as the etnachta.
The divine name is printed יְיָ.
The page ends mid-verse at 'בֶּן'.

blocks.text: Thou hast given us, O Lord our God, in love this day (of the Sabbath and this day) of remembrance, a day (of remembrance) of Teruah (in love) for a sacred convocation, a reminder of the exodus from Egypt.

Because of our sins we were exiled from our land and removed from our soil and we are unable to fulfil our duties in the House of Thy choice upon which Thy Name has been called, because of the hand that was stretched out against Thy sanctuary. May it be pleasing to Thee, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, O compassionate King, that Thou mayest again, in Thine abundant mercies, have compassion on us and on Thy sanctuary and rebuild it speedily and add to its glory. Our Father, our King, speedily reveal the glory of Thy Kingdom to us and appear and be exalted over us before the eyes of all the living. Bring near our dispersed ones from among the nations and collect our scattered ones from the corners of the earth and bring us to Zion, Thy city, in mirth, and to Jerusalem the House of Thy sanctuary, in eternal joy. There we will perform before Thee our sacrificial obligations, the regular offerings according to their order and the additional offerings according to their rule. And the additional offerings of this day of memorial we will prepare and offer up before Thee in love according to the commandment of Thy will as Thou hast written for us in Thy Torah through Moses Thy servant from Thy glorious mouth, saying:
uncertainties: The line break 'King-dom' is a printed hyphenation and is joined here.
The English leaves out the Shabbat insertion '(of this Sabbath and)' in the musaf sentence, even though the Hebrew has it.
Centered and printed in italics.
The opening parenthesis comes before this Hebrew word on the page: '(וביום'.

blocks.text: (On the Sabbath day two flawless lambs in their first year and two tenths of flour mixed with oil as a meal offering, and its drink offering. The Sabbath whole-offering on its Sabbath day in addition to the regular whole-offering and its drink offering.)
uncertainties: Printed in smaller type.

blocks.text: In the seventh month on the first day of the month you shall have a sacred assembly. You may not do any form of work, a day of Teruah shall it be for you. You shall prepare a whole-offering of sweet savour to the Lord, one young
uncertainties: The page ends mid-sentence at 'young'.

notes: Both scans are printed page 92: s204 is the Hebrew page and s205 is the facing English page.
For s205 I used only the full-page image. The English is clearly legible there, so I did not open the s205 enlarged bands.
There are no sound sequences, Hebrew-script German instructions or footnotes on these pages.

The Shabbat additions appear in two forms: short insertions in smaller type inside parentheses within the prayer text, and the Numbers 28:9–10 paragraph in parentheses after a small rubric. That rubric's Hebrew wording is uncertain; the English gives it as '(On the Sabbath)'.
Cantillation appears only on the Numbers 29:1–2 verse at the bottom of s204.
